content.text:
I made two interpretation errors.

First, I overcorrected away from `anyhow`: I prioritized retaining typed causes and turned `ApiError` into wrappers around `EntitySearchError` and `EntityDetailsError`. My [decision record](/tmp/exposed-http-tracing-design/design.md:71) explicitly chose those wrappers and removed the handler conversions. That was my design choice; your correction did not request it. The resulting [commit](https://github.com/johnnylarner/exposed/commit/e4f9be4078fc291391d259ac9bbee657d12a7f44) blurred the boundary you describe: `ApiError` should express HTTP outcomes and map domain failures into them. Preserving the original cause did not require replacing that role.

Second, I misunderstood “tracing macros” as the event macros `error!`, `warn!`, `info!`, and `debug!`. My [implementation notes](/tmp/exposed-http-tracing-design/design.md:114) record that interpretation. You meant attribute-based instrumentation—spelled [`#[tracing::instrument]`](https://docs.rs/tracing/0.1.44/tracing/attr.instrument.html). I found no record that I compared it with manual spans, so I cannot honestly claim that the manual implementation followed an evaluated tradeoff.

There is a relevant technical distinction, but it does not excuse that omission: `#[instrument]` creates spans; its optional `err` records returned errors. Using the attribute for context does not require logging the same propagated error at every layer. HTTP completion logging still needs an owner that sees response statuses and framework rejections.

[Issue #81](https://github.com/johnnylarner/exposed/issues/81) asks for original-error logging and generic public 500 responses. It does not prescribe domain wrappers or manual instrumentation. I satisfied parts of that behavior while making unnecessary architectural choices.

I checked Git history, PR #93, local design notes, and relevant GitHub issues. Those establish the misunderstanding; they contain no attribute-versus-manual comparison. Remote Drive was not relevant to these locally authored decisions. Team chat, observability, exception tracking, and analytics connectors were unavailable.
